newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: AMP's Ergo launches NZ on-call a/c, term deposits.
newsitem.headline: AMP's Ergo launches NZ on-call a/c, term deposits.

text.p: AMP Society's New Zealand telephone banking company Ergo Personal Services Ltd said it will launch an on-call account and a flexible range of term deposits on Wednesday.

"Traditionally the small investors (less than NZ$200,000 to invest) have missed out on higher interest rates, even though this group of customers makes up a large percentage of the investor market," Ergo said in a statement.
"By offering more competitive rates, no fees and more flexible terms on our deposit products we will encourage this group to start saving."
Ergo said the launch of deposit products was part of its commitment to compete vigorously with traditional banks.
At launch, interest on the call account would be around 4.55 percent for amounts less than $5,000 and 8.55 percent for amounts over $5,000.
Ergo said its term deposits were unique.
"Customers will not be restricted to the traditional 30, 60 and 90-day terms set by the banks," Ergo said.
The term deposit rates would range between 7.55 percent and 9.25 percent depending on the length of the deposit term.
As with all of Ergo's products, access is via the telephone because there is no extensive branch network.
Ergo was launched by AMP Society in November 1995.
While its share of New Zealand's financial services market was still small in comparison with the major players, Ergo said progress to date was pleasing.
"Direct banking is a new concept here, but New Zealanders are starting to realise that the industry is changing and they will benefit by shopping around for the best deal."
The on-call and term deposit rates would be reviewed daily and changed as required. -- Wellington Newsroom (64 4) 4734746
